subject: >>       1.  Vectorize the implementation of the transforms. >>           As is, they're just iterating, so a vector of positive >>           parameters (as in that compound K-distribution formulation) >>           is going to be dog slow. >> > By vectorize, do you mean checking to make sure the length of the vectors are all the same or one and then use vector > operations to carryout the transform?  I meant the efficient thing for derivatives -- define a new vari type (for reverse mode) for the Jacobian determinant.  This should be easy for the simple lower and upper bound constraints, but more involved for ordered vectors, unit-length vectors, and simplexes, and for covariance and correlation matrices. The implementation should look something like that of the distributions, as there may be vector inputs, but there's only a single return. If you can do more efficient implementations for forward-mode, that'd be good, too.  In fact, if you use OperandsAndPartials, you should be able to do both at the same time the way the distributions are being done now.  - Bob
